title: LLM Training Lifecycle: Pretraining → SFT → Preference Tuning
interviewAnswer: Modern LLM development commonly starts with next-token pretraining, then supervised instruction fine-tuning, and may add preference optimization such as RLHF or DPO. Each stage serves a different purpose.
why: This prevents mixing up pretraining, fine-tuning and alignment.
intuition: Pretraining learns broad language structure; SFT teaches task formats; preference tuning shifts behavior toward preferred outputs.
deepDive: Pretraining uses broad corpora and next-token likelihood; SFT uses curated prompt-response examples; preference stages optimize rankings/rewards.
commonMistakes: Assuming preference tuning reliably adds factual knowledge.
production: Dataset provenance and regression evaluation matter at every stage.
workedExample: A base model may autocomplete text, while an SFT model follows instructions more reliably.
